question: According to the Inter-Services Organisations (Command, Control and Discipline) Act, 2023—effective from May 2025—unified command authority has been granted over personnel from which branches of the Indian Armed Forces?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Army, Navy, and Air Force**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Inter-Services Organisations (Command, Control and Discipline) Act, 2023** enables the central government to provide unified command authority over personnel from the Army, Navy, and Air Force.
 
• Effective from **May 2025**, this act aims to enhance coordination, integration, and operational effectiveness across the three branches of the Indian Armed Forces.
 
• The act empowers the heads of inter-services organisations to exercise disciplinary and administrative control over personnel from different branches under their command.
 
• This legislation is a significant step towards achieving **jointness and synergy** in military operations, a crucial aspect of modern warfare.
 
• It facilitates the establishment of joint structures and commands, such as the Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) and integrated theatre commands, to streamline decision-making and execution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Navy and Air Force (Option 1):**

 
 
• The Navy and Air Force are two branches of the Indian Armed Forces, but the Inter-Services Organisations Act, 2023 focuses on **all three branches**, including the Army, to ensure unified command.
 
• While coordination between the Navy and Air Force is critical for maritime and aerial operations, unified authority is necessary to integrate all branches for comprehensive defense strategy.
 
 
 
• **Army and Navy (Option 2):**
 
 
• The Army and Navy operate in distinct domains—land and sea—and their integration is essential for coastal defense and amphibious operations.
 
• However, the Act includes the Air Force as well, making it inclusive of all major branches of the armed forces for effective joint operations.
 
 
 
• **Army and Coast Guard (Option 3):**
 
 
• The Coast Guard is not considered a part of the Indian Armed Forces but is a separate entity under the Ministry of Defence focused on maritime security and law enforcement.
 
• While coordination between the Army and Coast Guard is important in specific scenarios, the Act specifically addresses the Army, Navy, and Air Force for unified command structures.
 
 
 
• **Main Theme of the Question:**
 
 
• The Inter-Services Organisations (Command, Control and Discipline) Act, 2023 is a landmark legislation aimed at fostering **jointness and integration** among the Indian Armed Forces.
 
• It addresses long-standing issues of inter-service coordination and aims to enhance the nation’s defense preparedness through streamlined command structures.
 
• The Act is expected to play a pivotal role in modernizing the military and adapting to evolving security challenges.
